events.text: Pyo Danbi, who tells stories in the teahouse on Lantern Street for coppers, stops in the middle of a tale and points her fan at you. "You. You have been laughing at the right places all week. Sit with us." The table is a cooper, two sword students, a widow who sells dumplings and a scholar who failed the exams three times.

choices.text: Sit down and buy the first round

effects.log: You buy the round, and by the second pot of tea you know every name at the table.

choices.text: Tell them a story of your own

effects.log: Danbi listens with her head on one side, then laughs. "Competition," she says. You are in.

events.text: The circle has grown to a dozen. Wen the cooper comes to you white-faced: he borrowed from the Black Tiger moneylenders to save his workshop, and they want forty taels by the new moon or his hands.

choices.text: Pay the forty taels

effects.log: You count the silver into the moneylender's palm. Wen weeps into his sleeve all the way home.

choices.text: Gather the circle and pass the bowl

effects.log: Everyone gives what they can. It comes to thirty-eight taels, and you make up the rest.

choices.text: Tell him it is his own trouble

effects.log: Wen nods and does not come to the teahouse again. The circle is quieter for it.

events.text: The two sword students of the circle, Gil and Rho, have fallen out over the dumpling widow's daughter. Each wants you on his side; each says the other insulted him first. The whole of Lantern Street is waiting to see.

choices.text: Side with Gil

effects.log: Gil clasps your arm. Rho walks out, and three of the circle go after him.

choices.text: Bring them both to the same table

effects.log: It takes a whole night and two jars of wine. By dawn they are arguing about something else.

choices.text: Ask the daughter what she thinks

effects.log: She thinks they are both fools, and says so to their faces. The circle laughs for a week.

events.text: Rho's friends have started their own table across the street, and they toast loudly whenever you pass. Danbi says a street with two circles is a street with a war coming.

choices.text: Cross the street and drink with them

effects.log: You drink with them until they forget why they were angry. The street is one again.

choices.text: Let the street choose

effects.log: Half of Lantern Street stops coming to either table. You miss them.

events.text: Danbi is ill. The physician says it is the lungs, and that she should stop talking for a year. The storyteller laughs, coughs, and says that a year without talking would kill her faster.

choices.text: Take over her stories while she rests

effects.log: You tell her stories badly for a whole winter. The circle keeps coming anyway, for her.

choices.text: Pay for a mountain physician

effects.log: The physician from Mount Hua costs a great deal and is worth it. Danbi is back by spring, hoarse and furious.

events.text: Lantern Street holds its lantern festival, and the circle has a table at the front. Everyone you ever sat with comes: Wen with his new apprentice, Gil and Rho with their wives, the widow with her daughter, who married neither of them. Danbi stands up to tell the story of the circle, and it is about you.

choices.text: Stand up and toast them all

effects.log: You toast every one of them by name. Some of them cry. It is the best night of the year.

choices.text: Listen, and say nothing

effects.log: You let Danbi tell it. She gets half of it wrong, and you love her for every word.

events.text: A stranger at the inn is eating alone and looking at nobody. Before the soup is cold you know his name, his village, his trouble and his mother's cure for a cough.

choices.text: Invite him to travel with you as far as the next town

effects.log: He talks the whole way. You learn a road you did not know.

choices.text: Pay for his soup and leave him to it

effects.log: He looks up, surprised, and thanks you. That is enough.

events.text: A wedding in the village below. You know neither family, and by the end of the night you are leading the dance.

choices.text: Dance until the lanterns go out

effects.log: Both families claim you as a cousin by morning.

choices.text: Slip away before the speeches

effects.log: You leave them laughing. Somebody will tell the story of the stranger who danced.

events.text: An old sword master in the market has a crowd of children and nobody else. You start asking him questions, and by noon there are forty grown people listening too.

choices.text: Keep asking until he shows a real stance

effects.log: He shows one, grumbling, and you learn it with the children.

choices.text: Pass the hat for him

effects.log: The hat comes back heavy. He looks at you as if no one has been kind to him in years.

events.text: Above the last village, above the last shrine, there is a hut that belongs to nobody. Old Seo Mugyeong, who gathers herbs up there, says the last owner left it forty years ago and did not come back. It has a roof, a stove and a view of nothing but cloud.

choices.text: Take the hut for a season

effects.log: You carry up rice, oil and a single book. The silence is the best thing you have ever heard.

choices.text: Leave it as you found it

effects.log: You sit on its step for an afternoon, and go down lighter.

events.text: A boy comes up the path in the rain, lost and soaked, with a broken sandal. He says his name is Jun and his goats ran off. The hut has one blanket.

choices.text: Give him the blanket and the stove

effects.log: You sit up all night by the door. He snores. You do not mind as much as you thought.

choices.text: Walk him down to the village tonight

effects.log: It is a long walk in the rain, and he does not stop talking. At the bottom his mother bows to you twice.

events.text: Envoys from a sect three valleys away climb to the hut: their elder has heard of the one who sits above the clouds, and wants you at the sect for a teaching post. They have brought a sedan chair, which is absurd on this path.

choices.text: Go down with them for a year

effects.log: The sect is loud, and the students ask a thousand questions. You answer some of them.

choices.text: Send them back with a cup of tea each

effects.log: They drink the tea standing, go down, and tell everyone you are a recluse of great depth. You were only busy.

events.text: The year at the sect is over. A girl named Hyerin, the quietest of the students, asks if she can come up to the hut with you. She says she does not want to learn anything. She only wants to sit where it is quiet.

choices.text: Let her come

effects.log: She sits on the other side of the step and says nothing for a whole month. It is the best company you have had.

choices.text: Tell her to find her own hut

effects.log: She nods, as if she expected it, and finds one on the next peak. On clear days you see her smoke.

events.text: Old Seo Mugyeong has stopped coming up the path. You go down and find him in his house in the village, very old now, with nobody to bring him water. He says he would like to see the clouds once more.

choices.text: Carry him up on your back

effects.log: It takes all day. He sits on the step, looks at the cloud sea and says, "Yes. That is what it was for."

choices.text: Stay with him in the village to the end

effects.log: You fetch his water for a winter and listen to him. He dies in spring, holding your hand.

events.text: You have lived above the clouds long enough that the village children say you are a mountain spirit. One evening the sea of cloud below turns gold, and for a moment you understand something without words.

choices.text: Sit still and let it come

effects.log: It comes. It goes. Something in your qi has settled that will not unsettle again.

choices.text: Go down and tell somebody

effects.log: You find Jun, grown now, and try to tell him. He does not understand a word, and listens anyway.

events.text: The inn is full and the courtyard is full of drunk escort guards singing. You take your bowl to the stable and eat with the horses, who are better company.

choices.text: Sleep in the hayloft

effects.log: You sleep better than anyone in the inn.

choices.text: Walk on through the night

effects.log: The road is empty and the moon is good. You are at the next town by dawn.

events.text: Someone in the market recognises you and starts to wave. You turn down an alley before they reach you.

choices.text: Keep walking

effects.log: You are three streets away before you breathe again. There is a quiet temple there, and you sit in it.

choices.text: Go back and say hello after all

effects.log: It is an old acquaintance who only wanted to return a book. You feel a little foolish, and a little glad.

events.text: A season of snow closes the passes. Nobody can come up and nobody can go down, and you are delighted.

choices.text: Spend it on one technique

effects.log: By the thaw you know it better than its own master did.

choices.text: Spend it reading

effects.log: You read every book you carried up twice, and one of them three times.

events.text: Every morning there is a girl at the village well who is too small for the bucket. Her name is Ok-ja, she is about seven, and when you ask where her parents are she says "the fever" and nothing else.

choices.text: Carry her water home for her

effects.log: Home is a lean-to behind the granary. You carry the water, and then you carry rice.

choices.text: Find out who is meant to be looking after her

effects.log: An uncle, a drunkard, who has sold her blanket. You have words with him.

events.text: Ok-ja has the cough that took her parents. The village physician will not come to the lean-to for fear of it.

choices.text: Nurse her yourself

effects.log: Nine nights of boiling herbs and cold cloths. On the tenth she asks for a dumpling.

choices.text: Drag the physician there by the collar

effects.log: He comes, sulking, and his medicine works. He does not look you in the eye after.

events.text: A merchant couple from the next county, childless, have heard of the girl at the well and come to see her. They are kind and quite rich, and Ok-ja hides behind your legs.

choices.text: Let her choose

effects.log: She chooses to stay near you. The merchants leave silver for her schooling anyway.

choices.text: Persuade her to go with them

effects.log: She goes, crying, and writes to you every month in a hand that gets better and better.

events.text: Ok-ja is twelve now and has decided to learn the sword, because of you. She practises with a stick behind the granary and falls over a great deal.

choices.text: Teach her properly

effects.log: You teach her stances until she stops falling over. She is not gifted. She is stubborn, which is better.

choices.text: Teach her to read instead

effects.log: She is furious for a month, and then she reads everything in the village.

events.text: A letter in a fine hand: Ok-ja, at the merchant house, is to be married to a good young man and asks whether you will sit in her parents' place at the wedding.

choices.text: Go, in your best robe

effects.log: You sit in the parents' seat and she bows to you first. The merchant couple do not mind at all.

choices.text: Send a gift and your blessing

effects.log: You send a jade comb. She wears it at the wedding, and in every letter after.

events.text: Ok-ja, grown, opens a small house for orphans behind the granary where the lean-to used to be. She asks you to cut the ribbon on the door, and calls it the House at the Well.

choices.text: Cut the ribbon

effects.log: The children cheer. One of them is drawing water at the well this morning, and is too small for the bucket.

choices.text: Give it your silver

effects.log: You give it more than you meant to. It is the best silver you ever spent.

events.text: A stray dog follows you out of the town, limping. It has a thorn in its paw and an ear torn in a fight.

choices.text: Pull the thorn and feed it

effects.log: It follows you for three towns before it finds a butcher who likes it better.

choices.text: Carry it to the temple

effects.log: The monks take it in. It will be fat by summer.

events.text: An old woman is trying to drag a cart of firewood up the hill to her house. Nobody else on the road has stopped.

choices.text: Pull the cart for her

effects.log: Her house is a long way up. She gives you tea and a scolding for not eating enough.

choices.text: Pay a carter to do it every week

effects.log: You leave silver with the carter. She will not have to drag wood again this winter.

events.text: A young disciple in the inn has been crying into his bowl because he failed his sect's test.

choices.text: Sit with him and tell him about your own failures

effects.log: You tell him about every gate you failed. By the end he is laughing.

choices.text: Show him the move he failed on

effects.log: You show him on the inn table with chopsticks. He sees it, and runs out without paying.

events.text: Chae Gwangho sells secrets in the river ports, and he sold one of yours. You find him in a rice warehouse at night, counting his silver. He goes very pale.

choices.text: Make him kneel and count it out for you

effects.log: He counts it out on his knees. It comes to sixty taels, and the look on his face is worth more.

choices.text: Let him think you have forgiven him

effects.log: You smile and pour him wine. He will spend a year waiting for the knife.

choices.text: Let him go

effects.log: You let him go. It is not satisfying at all.

events.text: Chae Gwangho is afraid of you now, which makes him useful. He brings you a name: a magistrate's clerk who takes bribes and has a family he loves.

choices.text: Use the family to own the clerk

effects.log: The clerk does whatever you ask after you mention his daughter's school. You never even raise your voice.

choices.text: Make the clerk pay, and leave the family out of it

effects.log: He pays, every month. That is enough.

events.text: The river port has started to say your name in a low voice. A widow comes to you, not for help, but to ask you to leave her son alone: he owes the clerk money, and the clerk now owes you.

choices.text: Tell her the son will pay like everyone else

effects.log: She goes home. The son pays. The port grows quieter when you walk through it.

choices.text: Let the son off, this once

effects.log: She stares at you as if you were a ghost who had remembered something.

choices.text: Make the son work it off on your boats

effects.log: He works for a year. He does not smile once.

events.text: Chae Gwangho, more afraid than ever, has sold you to a rival in the ports: he gave them the place you sleep. You find out an hour before they come.

choices.text: Wait for them in the dark

effects.log: They come in, and you are waiting. By morning nobody in the port will take money against you again.

choices.text: Leave the port, and Chae with it

effects.log: You walk out with what you can carry. Somewhere behind you, the port finds a new thing to fear.

events.text: The widow's son, the one you let off, comes to you years later with a basket of river fish. He says he does not understand you, and does not want to, but thank you.

choices.text: Take the fish

effects.log: You take the fish. You eat it alone, and do not quite know what you feel.

choices.text: Send him away

effects.log: He goes. You are still yourself. It feels a little thinner than it did.

events.text: A beggar asks you for a copper and catches at your sleeve when you walk past.

choices.text: Kick his bowl into the gutter

effects.log: The coppers roll everywhere. You watch him crawl for them, and walk on.

choices.text: Drop him a copper

effects.log: He thanks you. You do not know why you did it.

choices.text: Shake him off and walk on

effects.log: You shake him off. He is already asking the next passer-by.

events.text: A rival's apprentice is caught in your courtyard, sent to spy. He is perhaps fifteen.

choices.text: Make an example of him in the market square

effects.log: You have him tied to the market post with a sign around his neck. His master does not send another.

choices.text: Send him home with a message

effects.log: You send him home with a message his master will not enjoy reading.

choices.text: Hire him

effects.log: He is astonished. He turns out to be a good apprentice.

events.text: You lose a spar in front of the sect courtyard to a younger disciple who did not even sweat.

choices.text: Make the next year of the disciple's life a small misery

effects.log: Spilled tea, lost manuals, the worst chores. The disciple never quite knows it is you.

choices.text: Ask the disciple how it was done

effects.log: The disciple shows you, shyly. You lose the next spar too, but more slowly.

events.text: In a ruined temple on the Yellow Road there is a monk called Baek Muyeom who does not pray. He says there is nothing to pray to and nobody to pray, and he sweeps the empty courtyard every morning anyway.

choices.text: Ask him why he sweeps, then

effects.log: "Because the leaves fall," he says. You sit with that for a long time.

choices.text: Tell him you already knew there was nothing

effects.log: He smiles, for the first time. "Then you can help me sweep."

events.text: It is the spring festival and the whole town is out with paper lanterns. You walk through it and feel nothing at all, as if the lanterns were painted on a wall.

choices.text: Go back to the temple and sweep

effects.log: Baek Muyeom hands you the broom without a word. The leaves, at least, are real.

choices.text: Light a lantern anyway

effects.log: It floats up and goes out. You watch it the whole way. That was something, perhaps.

events.text: An old friend of your childhood, Jo Hana, finds you and asks you straight out: what is the point of all your cultivation, if nothing matters? She is crying, because her child died in the winter.

choices.text: Tell her the truth as you see it

effects.log: You tell her there is no point. She hits you, hard, and then holds on to you and weeps.

choices.text: Tell her it matters because she cared

effects.log: You do not believe it when you say it. She does, and that is enough for tonight.

choices.text: Say nothing, and stay

effects.log: You say nothing and stay all night. In the morning she says it helped.

events.text: Baek Muyeom is dying. He lies on the temple floor and asks you whether, after all, you found anything.

choices.text: Say no

effects.log: "Good," he says. "Then nobody can take it from you." He dies smiling at the roof.

choices.text: Say: the sweeping

effects.log: He laughs until he coughs. "Yes. The sweeping." It is the last thing he says.

events.text: Jo Hana has a new child, and she brings the baby to the ruined temple to show you. She says you were the only one who did not tell her it would be all right.

choices.text: Hold the baby

effects.log: The baby grabs your finger. It is a very small thing, and it does not let go.

choices.text: Bless it in the old way

effects.log: You do not believe in the blessing. You say it carefully anyway, every word.

events.text: A merchant is weeping because his ship sank with all his cargo.

choices.text: Tell him it would have rotted one day anyway

effects.log: He stops weeping and stares at you. Then, oddly, he laughs.

choices.text: Buy him a drink

effects.log: He drinks it. Nothing is fixed. Something is a little better.

events.text: You reach a new realm, and the morning after you cannot remember why you wanted it.

choices.text: Train anyway

effects.log: Without wanting, the training goes strangely well.

choices.text: Spend a day doing nothing

effects.log: You lie in the grass all day. A cloud looks like nothing at all.

events.text: Children in the village are playing at being great heroes of the murim, with sticks.

choices.text: Tell them how heroes really end

effects.log: They listen with round eyes and go home quieter. One of them cries.

choices.text: Play the villain for them

effects.log: You fall down dead nine times. They are delighted.

events.text: Gong Sori runs a troupe of six jugglers and one bad-tempered donkey, and her cart has lost a wheel in the mud. You laugh, and she laughs, and by the time the wheel is back on you have agreed to walk with them to the coast.

choices.text: Learn to juggle on the way

effects.log: You drop everything for three days, and then you do not. The donkey is unimpressed.

choices.text: Play the drum for them

effects.log: You play the drum badly and loudly. The crowds love it.

events.text: The troupe comes to a town where nobody has laughed since the flood took the market. The people stand in the square and watch the jugglers with dead eyes.

choices.text: Fall off the stage on purpose

effects.log: You fall off the stage four times. On the fourth, a child laughs, and then the whole square does.

choices.text: Help them rebuild the market stalls first

effects.log: You spend a week with a hammer. When the troupe performs, the town comes to the new stalls to watch.

events.text: Bandits stop the troupe on the coast road: nine of them, hungry, with rusty sabres. Their leader wants the cart, the donkey and the drum.

choices.text: Offer to perform for them instead

effects.log: You do the whole show on the road. The bandits laugh until they weep, and let you pass with a bag of their dried fish.

choices.text: Draw your sword, smiling

effects.log: You fight them off without ever stopping smiling, which frightens them more than the blade.

events.text: Gong Sori is getting old, and the troupe needs someone to lead it. She hands you the drumsticks in front of everyone.

choices.text: Take the troupe

effects.log: You lead the troupe for a season. It is chaos. It is wonderful.

choices.text: Give the sticks to the youngest juggler

effects.log: Little Mae nearly drops them, and then holds them up like a sword. The troupe cheers.

events.text: Years later, in a city far from the coast, you hear a drum played badly and loudly in a square. It is Mae's troupe, and they still do your fall off the stage.

choices.text: Climb up and do it yourself

effects.log: You fall off the stage once more. Your knees complain. The crowd roars.

choices.text: Watch from the back, grinning

effects.log: You watch the whole show and leave a silver tael in the hat.

events.text: Rain on the road, mud to the ankles, and the inn is full. You start laughing and cannot stop.

choices.text: Sing in the rain

effects.log: A farmer hears you and offers his barn, because anyone singing in that is either mad or good company.

choices.text: Sleep under a cart, cheerfully

effects.log: You wake soaked and laughing. A child gives you a warm bun for no reason.

events.text: Your breakthrough fails, and you sit in the wreck of your meditation room and laugh at yourself.

choices.text: Try again tomorrow

effects.log: You try again tomorrow, lighter. The qi is calmer for it.

choices.text: Go out for noodles

effects.log: The noodles are excellent. The gate will still be there.

events.text: A grim old elder in the inn says there is nothing to smile about in the murim.

choices.text: Make him smile anyway

effects.log: It takes the whole evening. You get one smile, small and rusty, and he pays for your supper.

choices.text: Agree with him, smiling

effects.log: He glares, and then, unwillingly, laughs.

events.text: The river at Willow Crossing is high for the season, and you do not like the colour of the sky. Old Min Dalgu the ferryman agrees with you. Nobody else in the town does.

choices.text: Start moving grain to the hill granary

effects.log: The townsfolk laugh at you, carrying sacks uphill in the sun. You carry them anyway.

choices.text: Warn the headman

effects.log: The headman says you worry too much. Min Dalgu says you do not worry enough.

events.text: The rains come in the night, as you said they would, and the river comes over the banks. Half the town is on the roofs by dawn.

choices.text: Take Min Dalgu's ferry through the streets

effects.log: You row all day. You bring forty people to the hill, where your grain is waiting.

choices.text: Hold the granary door against the panic

effects.log: You keep order at the granary while the town comes up the hill wet and terrified. Nobody fights over the rice.

events.text: The headman, who laughed, comes to you after the flood with his hat in his hands. The town wants you to plan for the next one.

choices.text: Draw them a dyke and a flood road

effects.log: You draw every bad thing that could happen. They build for all of it.

choices.text: Tell them it will be worse next time

effects.log: They believe you this time. It is not as satisfying as you hoped.

events.text: The next flood comes, smaller than the first. The dyke holds. People thank you in the street, and you cannot help thinking of the one that will break it.

choices.text: Go and check the dyke in the rain

effects.log: You find the weak place and plug it before morning. It would have gone, you are sure.

choices.text: Let yourself, just once, be pleased

effects.log: You drink with Min Dalgu at the ferry. He says it is the first time he has seen you smile.

events.text: Min Dalgu is dying, and he asks you what you think comes after.

choices.text: Tell him nothing good

effects.log: "Then we were right all along," he says, pleased. He dies holding your sleeve.

choices.text: Tell him something kind, for once

effects.log: He looks at you sideways. "You have gone soft." He dies smiling anyway.

events.text: A friend is about to marry. You can see three ways it goes wrong.

choices.text: Tell them

effects.log: They do not thank you. Two of the three ways happen anyway. They come back, years later, and do thank you.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself and give a good gift

effects.log: It goes well, against every expectation of yours.

events.text: The road ahead looks wrong to you: too quiet, a broken branch, no birds.

choices.text: Take the long way round

effects.log: You hear later that bandits were waiting in the trees for a whole day.

choices.text: Go on with a hand on your hilt

effects.log: Nothing happens. You are almost disappointed.

events.text: Everyone in the sect is excited for the tournament. You expect to lose in the first round.

choices.text: Train twice as hard because of it

effects.log: You lose in the second round, which is better than you feared.

choices.text: Do not go at all

effects.log: You spend the tournament in the library. Nobody notices you there, and you read a great deal.

events.text: Jegal Wonsu, young master of the Jegal family, laughs at you in the Golden Crane restaurant: "That one? I could beat that one with chopsticks." Every table goes quiet.

choices.text: Pick up a pair of chopsticks and stand

effects.log: You stand, chopsticks in hand. "Show me," you say. The whole restaurant holds its breath.

choices.text: Laugh louder than he did

effects.log: You laugh at him until he goes red. Half the restaurant laughs with you.

choices.text: Ignore him

effects.log: You eat your noodles. It is the hardest thing you have done all year.

events.text: The duel with Jegal Wonsu is set for the square outside the Golden Crane, and half the city has come. He has brought his family's best sword. You have brought your reputation.

choices.text: Duel him seriously

ok.log: You disarm him in seven moves and hand the sword back to him by the blade. The square erupts.

fail.log: He is better than you thought. You lose in front of the whole city, and walk home very slowly.

choices.text: Beat him with one hand behind your back

ok.log: You do it. Nobody in the city will ever forget it, least of all him.

fail.log: The hand behind your back was a mistake. The whole city saw exactly how big a mistake.

events.text: Jegal Wonsu's uncle, the family head, sends a polite letter that is not polite at all. You humiliated his heir. The Jegal family would like an apology, in public.

choices.text: Refuse, in public

effects.log: You read the letter aloud in the Golden Crane and tear it in half. The Jegal family will not forget.

choices.text: Apologise, gracefully

effects.log: It costs you more than any wound. The family head bows back. Strangely, people respect you more for it.

events.text: After the defeat, Jegal Wonsu comes to your door. He does not gloat. He says: you are not bad, you only fight as if everyone is watching. He offers to spar again, privately.

choices.text: Accept, and fight as if nobody is watching

effects.log: Nobody is watching. You learn more in that one spar than in a year of duels.

choices.text: Slam the door

effects.log: You slam the door. He laughs on the other side of it, and goes.

events.text: Years on, you and Jegal Wonsu meet in the same Golden Crane. He is head of his family now.

choices.text: Buy him a drink

effects.log: He drinks it. "Chopsticks," he says, and you both laugh until the waiters stare.

choices.text: Remind him who won

effects.log: He sets the cup down. "Still," he says, and leaves. Some things do not change.

events.text: A tournament herald reads out the names of the young talents of the province. Yours is fifth.

choices.text: Go and correct him

effects.log: You correct him in front of the crowd. It is a little embarrassing. Next year you are third.

choices.text: Challenge the fourth name

effects.log: The fourth name accepts. The crowd loves it.

events.text: A proud old master in the sect looks at your stance and sniffs.

choices.text: Tell him what you think of his stance

effects.log: You tell him. He turns purple. The other disciples will talk about it for years.

choices.text: Bow and ask what is wrong

effects.log: He tells you, at length. He is right, irritatingly.

events.text: A crowd gathers when you walk into the city. Someone has heard of you.

choices.text: Stop and let them look

effects.log: You stop and let them look. A poet writes a bad verse about you that is sung for a season.

choices.text: Walk faster

effects.log: You walk faster. They follow anyway.

events.text: Do Yeongsu, captain of the Blue Horse caravan, hires you as a guard for the Red Pass road. On the first evening you stop at the fork and do not like what you see: fresh hoofprints, no birds, a branch broken at the height of a rider.

choices.text: Tell the captain to take the low road

effects.log: Yeongsu grumbles about the lost day and takes it. At the inn that night you hear the high road was full of bandits.

choices.text: Scout ahead alone first

effects.log: You find eleven men waiting in the trees, and come back without being seen.

events.text: An inn at the halfway town. The soup smells wrong to you: something bitter under the pepper. The innkeeper smiles too much.

choices.text: Knock the bowls out of everyone's hands

effects.log: The guards are furious, and then the cook runs. The soup was full of sleeping powder.

choices.text: Pretend to eat and watch

effects.log: You watch the guards go sleepy, and you are awake when the innkeeper's friends come in. They do not expect that.

events.text: The caravan reaches the river ferry. The ferryman wants double, the river is high, and a stranger offers a shortcut over an old rope bridge.

choices.text: Pay the ferryman double

effects.log: It is expensive and slow and nothing goes wrong at all, which is exactly what you wanted.

choices.text: Test the rope bridge first with a sack

effects.log: The sack goes halfway and the bridge goes with it. The stranger is gone when you turn round.

events.text: At the end of the road Do Yeongsu counts his cargo: all of it, every horse, every guard alive. He has never done the Red Pass without losing someone. He offers you a share of the caravan.

choices.text: Take the share

effects.log: You become a partner in the Blue Horse caravan. You check every road twice for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Take only your wage

effects.log: You take your wage and go. Yeongsu sends you a jar of wine every new year.

events.text: A young guard of the Blue Horse, Sihu, who laughed at you on the Red Pass, comes to ask how you knew.

choices.text: Teach him to read a road

effects.log: You teach him the birds, the branches, the smell of a trap. He becomes the best scout the caravan ever had.

choices.text: Tell him you just worry

effects.log: He does not believe you. That is the first lesson.

events.text: Your breakthrough feels ready. Everything says go. Something small says wait.

choices.text: Wait a season

effects.log: You wait. When you finally go in, the qi is as calm as a pond.

choices.text: Go now

effects.log: You go now. It is fine. You were right to worry anyway.

events.text: A cave on the mountain, with an old inscription promising a hidden art.

choices.text: Light a fire at the mouth and watch the smoke

effects.log: The smoke is drawn into the cave and out through a crack: there is a pit inside. You go round it.

choices.text: Go in at once

effects.log: You go in carefully, which is just as well. The second step is not there.

events.text: A stranger in the inn offers you a share in a deal that cannot fail.

choices.text: Ask a great many questions

effects.log: He leaves before you are halfway through them.

choices.text: Ask the innkeeper about him

effects.log: The innkeeper laughs. The man has been selling the same deal for ten years.

events.text: At Willow Ford the Demonic Cult has taken the village granary and the headman's son. The widow Han Seol, who runs the ferry, says the sects will not come because the village is too poor to pay.

choices.text: Go to the granary tonight

effects.log: You go to the granary tonight. The cultists are not expecting anyone at all.

choices.text: Gather the village men first

effects.log: You drill them with hoes and poles for three days. Then you go together.

events.text: The Cult does not forget. Its envoy, a soft-voiced man in black named Ma Gyeol, comes to the ford alone and offers you silver to go away, or the village burns at the next moon.

choices.text: Throw the silver in the river

effects.log: The silver sinks. Ma Gyeol watches it go with interest. "As you like," he says.

choices.text: Seize the envoy as a hostage

effects.log: You take him. He comes quietly, which worries you.

events.text: The Cult comes at the next moon: thirty of them, with torches. Han Seol's ferry is the only way across, and the village is on the far bank.

choices.text: Hold the ferry landing alone

ok.log: You hold the landing until dawn. The Cult goes back into the hills, and the village is still there.

fail.log: You are driven back to the water, wounded, but the village has had the time it needed to flee across.

choices.text: Cut the ferry rope and take the village up the hill

effects.log: The Cult stands on the far bank shouting. The village is safe, and the ferry is gone.

events.text: A sect of the Orthodox Alliance, hearing too late, sends disciples to the ford to take the credit. Their senior, Namgung Do, wants your name off the story.

choices.text: Let them have it

effects.log: The story becomes theirs. The village knows the truth, and that is the part that matters.

choices.text: Tell the truth to the whole province

effects.log: You tell it. The Alliance is embarrassed, and the next poor village that calls, they come.

events.text: Han Seol, grey now, sends word that the Cult is moving in the hills again, and that she is too old to run the ferry.

choices.text: Go back to the ford

effects.log: You go back to the ford. The Cult, hearing who has come, decides it has business elsewhere.

choices.text: Send the best student you have

effects.log: You send your best student with a letter. Han Seol writes back: a good one.

events.text: A magistrate's men are beating a peddler in the market for a tax he has already paid.

choices.text: Step between them

effects.log: You step between them. The magistrate's men think better of it.

choices.text: Pay the tax again for him

effects.log: You pay it. The peddler presses a fan on you in thanks.

choices.text: Walk on

effects.log: You walk on. The sound follows you down the street.

events.text: A disciple of the Demonic Cult, wounded, begs you for water on the road.

choices.text: Give water, and then take him to the magistrate

effects.log: He drinks, and goes with you without a word.

choices.text: Give water and let him go

effects.log: He goes. You do not know if you were right. You think you were.

events.text: Your own sect has quietly taken a farmer's field for a new training ground.

choices.text: Speak against it at the sect assembly

effects.log: You speak. The elders are cold to you for a year. The farmer gets his field back.

choices.text: Pay the farmer out of your own purse

effects.log: You pay him. It is not justice, but it is something.

choices.text: Keep your head down

effects.log: You keep your head down. The new training ground is very fine, and you never enjoy it.

events.text: Gu Yeonbok, steward of a great sect's treasury, keeps two ledgers. You know because his clerk drinks, and talks. The second ledger is in the false bottom of his desk.

choices.text: Copy the second ledger

effects.log: You copy it by candlelight, page by page, and are gone before the watch changes.

choices.text: Steal it outright

effects.log: You take it. By morning the whole treasury is in uproar, and Gu Yeonbok is very quiet.

events.text: Gu Yeonbok receives a letter with a single page of his own ledger in it, and an invitation to tea.

choices.text: Ask for silver every season

effects.log: He pays every season. He hates you quietly and very efficiently.

choices.text: Ask for a post in the treasury instead

effects.log: He gives you a post. Now you can see everything.

choices.text: Sell the page to his rival

effects.log: His rival pays well. Gu Yeonbok is gone from the treasury by autumn.

events.text: From your post in the treasury you can see who is paying whom across three sects and a magistrate's court. It is like reading a game of baduk from above.

choices.text: Move one piece: arrange a marriage alliance

effects.log: You arrange it with three letters and a dinner. Two sects bind themselves together, and both owe you.

choices.text: Move nothing yet, and keep watching

effects.log: You keep watching. Patience is also a move.

events.text: Gu Yeonbok has found out who you are. He has hired someone. You hear of it from the same drunk clerk, who is now more frightened of you than of the steward.

choices.text: Expose the ledger to the sect elders first

effects.log: The elders take him away before his hired blade arrives. Nobody asks how you knew.

choices.text: Pay the hired blade more

effects.log: The blade takes your silver and goes home. Gu Yeonbok waits for a long time.

events.text: In the end everyone wonders about you. The elders smile at you and count their spoons when you leave.

choices.text: Do one honest thing, loudly

effects.log: You return a lost purse in front of the whole hall. Nobody believes it was honest, which is very funny.

choices.text: Enjoy it

effects.log: You enjoy it very much.

events.text: Two elders of the sect both want the same disciple for their hall.

choices.text: Tell each of them the other is going to win

effects.log: Both outbid each other for your support. The disciple goes to the one who paid you more.

choices.text: Tell the disciple to choose

effects.log: The disciple chooses, and is grateful to you for asking.

events.text: A clerk at the magistrate's court is selling his master's secrets to anyone who pays.

choices.text: Buy them all, and sell them back to the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate pays twice what you did, and owes you a favour besides.

choices.text: Report the clerk

effects.log: The clerk is thrown out. The magistrate remembers your name.

events.text: People have begun to lower their voices when you come into a room.

choices.text: Lower yours too

effects.log: Now they wonder what you are saying. It is mostly about the weather.

choices.text: Bring a cake

effects.log: You bring a cake. They eat it suspiciously, and then with pleasure.

events.text: A rich merchant's son has run over a farmer's child with his cart and is laughing about it in the inn.

choices.text: Learn his father's secrets and make the father pay

effects.log: The father pays you handsomely to keep quiet, and the child's family a little.

choices.text: Break the cart in front of him

effects.log: You break his cart over your knee. He stops laughing. Everyone does.

choices.text: Carry the child to the physician yourself

effects.log: You run the whole way with the child in your arms. The child will walk again.

choices.text: Look away

effects.log: You look away. The laughing goes on behind you all the way to the door.

events.text: An enemy of yours lies sick with fever in an inn on the road, with no servant and no silver.

choices.text: Make sure he knows you saw him like this

effects.log: You stand at the foot of his bed until he sees you. Then you leave. He will remember that look for life.

choices.text: Pay for his room and leave before he wakes

effects.log: You pay and go. He will never know, and that is fine.

choices.text: Walk on

effects.log: You walk on. It is not your business.

events.text: A sect elder offers you a shortcut: a pill that will open your next gate early, made from a beast nobody is meant to hunt.

choices.text: Ask where exactly it came from, and who else has taken one

effects.log: Three of the five who took one went mad. You hand it back, very politely.

choices.text: Take it and throw it in his face

effects.log: "Do you know who I am?" you say. It turns out he does now. So does the whole hall.

choices.text: Decline

effects.log: You decline. He shrugs and offers it to someone else.

choices.text: Take it

effects.log: You take it. It burns going down, and something in your qi is not quite yours afterwards.

events.text: A widow's house is to be seized by a moneylender who forged her husband's debt.

choices.text: Find the forger and make him confess in the market

effects.log: You find him. He confesses loudly. The moneylender leaves town.

choices.text: Forge a better paper of your own

effects.log: Your paper says the moneylender owes her. The magistrate believes yours.

choices.text: Buy the debt and burn it

effects.log: You buy it and burn it in front of her. She cannot speak.

choices.text: Leave it to the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate takes his time. The house is lost.

events.text: A young cultivator challenges you on the road, too young and too sure.

choices.text: Beat him badly enough that he never forgets

effects.log: He limps home and never draws on a stranger again. Perhaps that saved his life. Perhaps not.

choices.text: Beat him, and tell everyone

effects.log: You win, and make sure the next town hears exactly how.

choices.text: Teach him something instead

effects.log: You show him one thing he did wrong. He goes home thoughtful.

choices.text: Decline and walk on

effects.log: He calls you a coward. You do not mind.

events.text: Rain at a mountain shrine, and a stranger already sheltering there, with a heavy bundle and a frightened face.

choices.text: Watch his hands before you sit

effects.log: His hand goes to a knife inside the bundle when you come in. You sit where he cannot reach you, and both of you live till morning.

choices.text: Ask about his family

effects.log: He has three children waiting. By morning you have given him your spare rice.

choices.text: Share the fire

effects.log: You share the fire and say little. In the morning he is gone, and so is the rain.
